name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
state_or_region: Tennessee & North Carolina (Great Smoky Mountains National Park)
agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
summary: The whole of America's most-visited national park: misty ridges along the Appalachian Trail from Fontana Dam to Davenport Gap, Clingmans Dome and Mount Le Conte, old-growth coves, waterfalls, Cades Cove and Cataloochee.

pois.name: Clingmans Dome
pois.note: Highest point in the park and in Tennessee (6,643 ft); observation tower

pois.name: Mount Le Conte
pois.note: Third-highest peak in the Smokies; LeConte Lodge just below the summit

pois.name: LeConte Lodge
pois.note: Hike-in lodge (reservations); reached only on foot

pois.name: Newfound Gap
pois.note: Appalachian Trail crossing of US 441 on the TN/NC line

pois.name: Charlies Bunion
pois.note: Rocky outcrop on the Appalachian Trail with sheer drop-offs

pois.name: Alum Cave Trailhead
pois.note: US 441: Arch Rock, Inspiration Point and Alum Cave Bluffs on the way to Mount Le Conte

pois.name: Sugarlands Visitor Center
pois.note: Main Tennessee visitor center near Gatlinburg

pois.name: Oconaluftee Visitor Center
pois.note: North Carolina visitor center near Cherokee

pois.name: Cades Cove Visitor Center
pois.note: Historic valley on the 11-mile loop road

pois.name: Laurel Falls
pois.note: Paved, very busy trail from Fighting Creek Gap

pois.name: Ramsey Cascades
pois.note: Tallest waterfall in the park, in old-growth forest

pois.name: Mount Cammerer Lookout
pois.note: Stone fire lookout at the park's northeast corner

pois.name: Gregory Bald
pois.note: Grassy bald famous for its June flame azaleas

pois.name: Fontana Dam
pois.note: Southern entry of the Appalachian Trail into the park

pois.name: Cataloochee Valley
pois.note: Remote historic valley; elk often in the fields at dawn and dusk
